messages:
maria: heads up — our quota graphs are double-counting requests for some customers. console shows consumption under 'org default' AND under project id when x-origin headers are present. noticed after the last rollout.

alex: ack. do you have an example request?

maria: pasted one from staging logs:

```
POST /v1/generate
Headers: {
  Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx,
  x-redwood-org: org_123,
  x-redwood-project: proj_789
}
Body: {...}
```

But telemetry pipeline emits meter:org=org_123 and meter:project=missing (falls back to org) and a second metric where origin=sk_live_xxx -> counts again. so two distinct series that the console sums.

jin: that sounds like the request attribution fallthrough + token-origin fallback we have. metrics pipeline currently tags by: project if present else org, and also by token-origin (key). the console aggregation is naive and treats them as separate buckets.

sam: either we canonicalize in pipeline (preferred) or we teach console to roll up by canonical attribution. pipeline change will reduce cardinality though.

alex: what's the perf/cost impact? pipeline dedupe means a join on request id or using single attribution stage — might add 10-20% cost to telemetry processing.

maria: cost is acceptable for canary. main worry is correctness for billing and SLO dashboards — customers see >100% of committed quota.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: telemetry-pipeline v2 at canary-3 (10% of traffic).

jin: propose this quick fix for canary: 1) pipeline emits canonical_attr = project if project present else org; 2) still emit token_origin for debug but mark as debug=true; 3) console aggregation uses canonical_attr by default and exposes token_origin as optional breakdown.

sam: sounds good. will need a console flag and a backfill plan for historical charts (we can map historical metrics to canonical_attr during query time).

alex: small UX ask — show an orange badge on graphs when debug token_origin breakdown is active so CS doesn't get alarmed.

maria: agreed. rollout plan: canary now, monitor three dashboards (quota-usage, sso-sample, account-billing), if 24h stable -> promote. I'll open a short PR for pipeline change and a console flag PR.

alex: add a telemetry test: send synthetic request with both headers + token, assert single canonical series increments by 1.

maria: adding test to the PR. pinging @jin @sam for reviews. :thumbsup:

observability-bot: alert muted for quota-duplication until 1695580000 per maria.

jin: one more note — for legacy keys without project binding we should keep token-origin breakdown visible, but not included in billing queries. document in runbook.

sam: i'll add runbook section and update the canary checklist.

maria: thanks all — i'll open the PRs and post links in this thread.

alex: ty!
